about.ru: Припев Sweet Georgia Brown (1925) по первому изданию, перенесён из G в F. Аккорды идут по кругу: D7, G7, C7, F.
about.en: The chorus of Sweet Georgia Brown (1925) from the first edition, moved from G to F. The chords go round the circle: D7, G7, C7, F.

source: Ben Bernie / Maceo Pinkard / Kenneth Casey, Sweet Georgia Brown, Jerome H. Remick & Co., New York / Detroit, 1925, first edition with ukulele arrangement (IMSLP #718454), chorus, vocal line and ukulele chord symbols, transposed from G to F; public domain
notes: KEY: the 1925 edition prints the chorus in G major (one sharp; chords E7 A7 D7 G). It is transposed here down a whole tone to F major (E7->D7, A7->G7, D7->C7, G->F, Em7->Dm7, B7->A7, Em->Dm) to fit the form sgb-f; all pitches below are the transposed ones. Raised chromatic notes are spelled as sharps (F#4, C#5), as printed (G#, D#) in the original.
Source pages: chorus = PDF pages 4-5 (printed pages 4 and 5), cut time read as 8 eighths per bar. 32 bars: page 4 = 16 bars (4 systems x 4), page 5 = 4 + 5 + 4 + 3 bars including the endings.

Bars 12 and 14: the edition prints D7 then '(D7+5)' over beat 4 (original key); the vocabulary has no +5, so both bars are 'C7' (augmented fifth dropped). Bar 14: the printed G of bar 13 still sounds under the tied first beat; D7 is printed from beat 2, so bar 14 is just 'C7'.
Bar 15: printed G on beat 1 and '(Em7)' over beat 4 only; a beat-4 chord cannot be expressed (two chords split at beat 3), so bar 15 is 'F' and the Dm7 (Em7 in G) passing chord is dropped.
Bars 15-16 ('Not much!') are marked '(spoken ad lib)' in the edition; the printed pitches are kept (A4 quarter, then G4 dotted half).
Bar 24: printed A7 (carried from bar 21) for the held note, then '(B7)' over the half rest on beat 3 -> 'G7 A7'.
Bar 31: printed A7 on beat 1 and D7 on beat 3 -> 'G7 C7'.

Bar 32: the chorus has 1st/2nd endings; the 2nd (final) ending is used. 1st ending = G (beat 1), B7 (beat 3) -> 'F A7' in F, the turnaround back to the top that a looping form would normally use. 2nd ending prints G, D7 (beat 3), G (beat 4) -> 'F'; the passing C7 (D7 in G) is dropped.

Bar 32 rhythm anomaly: the 2nd ending prints a half note tied to an eighth on the and-of-4 plus an eighth rest = only 6 eighths. No note is invented: the tied tone is rendered as one held F4 (t0, 7 eighths, tied from bar 31) followed by the eighth rest.

Chord symbols as printed (normalized only by transposition): plain triads stay plain ('F', 'Dm'), dominant sevenths '7'. Chords not printed in a bar carry over the last printed one (bars 2-4, 6-8, 10-11, 18-20, 22-23 follow the chord printed at the start of the 4-bar group).
D.S. after the 2nd ending returns to the segno at the start of the verse (page 2); not relevant to the chorus transcription.
Fingerings are editorial (not in the source).
